local_articles.title: Neeraj Chopra to miss Asian Games for India after suffering ligament tear: ‘I will sit out the rest of this season’
local_articles.snippet: Neeraj Chopra on Saturday confirmed that he would miss the upcoming Diamond League final in Brussels and the Asian Games after getting injured. The two-time Olympic medallist took to Instagram to confirm that he suffered a ligament tear in his ankle during a training session and would therefore miss the remainder of the 2026 season. local_articles.title: Troy Parrott to make first La Liga start for Real Betis
local_articles.snippet: Republic of Ireland international Troy Parrott is set to make his first start for Real Betis later today. The Dubliner, who signed for Manuel Pellegrini’s side last week following a deal reportedly worth €20 million, has been named in the starting XI for their away fixture against Levante in La Liga. The game in Valencia kicks off at 4pm Irish time. Parrott made his first appearance for the Spanish club earlier this week, coming on as a substitute in their 1-0 away win over Valencia. Sprung from the bench in the 70th minute, the 24-year-old quickly made his presence felt, pulling a shot wide before being involved in the build-up to Pablo García 83th-minute winner.

questions.title: Which bank will the U.S. Treasury sanction over alleged financial ties to Iran during August 31–September 6, 2026?
questions.background: The United States uses financial sanctions to restrict institutions accused of helping Iran access the international financial system.

questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-28 Treasury action clarifies Operation Economic Outcast targeting just before the Aug 31-Sept 6 window: FinCEN proposed a Section 311 special measure (30-day public comment period, explicitly not an OFAC asset-blocking designation) against the UAE branches of Egypt's Banque Misr over $1.8B in alleged Iran shadow-banking flows, while OFAC sanctioned Bank Melli's Dubai branch GM and a Hong Kong trading firm. Because the Banque Misr FinCEN proposal was announced on Aug 28 (outside the Aug 31-Sept 6 window), next week's OFAC bank designation will almost certainly target another lender. Crucially, FT, Iran International, CNBC TV18, and Arab News (Aug 28) all emphasize Washington's continued reluctance to sanction major Chinese G-SIBs ahead of President Xi Jinping's September US visit—instead hitting non-systemic regional intermediaries (with Treasury's Aug 28 press release also flagging Iranian proxy funding in Iraq). Accordingly, we cut major Chinese banks (Bank of China 0.035 -> 0.02, dropping ICBC), nudge up Iraqi state banks repeatedly scrutinized for Iran USD/militia conduits (Rafidain Bank 0.09 -> 0.10, Trade Bank of Iraq 0.04 -> 0.045, Rasheed Bank 0.03 -> 0.035), and add Turkey's Halkbank (0.02), keeping total top-5 mass disciplined at 0.22 across a wide global banking field.
